summary: AVONET (figshare 16586228 v7, CC BY 4.0) gives body mass and wing linear measures for every bird species but no wing area, flight speed or muscle mass. Per-species flight speeds exist only in paper supplements (Alerstam et al. 2007 was not found as a repository dataset), Movebank tracks require a login to list, and flight-muscle mass is scattered across single-species deposits; the closest comparative proxy found is a sternum-morphology dataset (10.5061/dryad.x3ffbg7jj).
next_step: Compile a species table joining AVONET mass and wing measures with Alerstam 2007 radar speeds and a flight-muscle-mass compilation (e.g. from Wright et al. 2016 or Greenewalt 1962), then pre-register the exponent tests (speed ~ L^0.5, required power ~ L^3.5, muscle ~ L^3).
obstacles_confirmed: Flight power and muscle power are seldom directly measured in open comparative datasets: no multi-species flight-muscle or power table surfaced.
External morphology does not contain muscle mass or measured flight power: AVONET confirms this.
Movebank requires authentication even to list studies (HTTP 401).
